---
title: Build a Raycast extension
description: Write a small Raycast extension that saves a file from your Mac to your instance, with a key of its own that can write files and nothing else.
---

- **You'll build** a Raycast extension with one command, **Save File**. It shows a form where you pick a file, uploads its bytes to your instance and saves it as a file item.
- **You need** your own Marfa instance, with the CLI signed in to it, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you, plus [Raycast](https://www.raycast.com) and [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.14 or later on a Mac.
- **You'll have** a command that saves any file on your Mac to Marfa. [Build forms from types in a Raycast extension](/build/raycast-type-forms) adds a second command to it.

An extension is a client of your instance, like any app you write. It sends requests with a key, and the key decides what it may do. Here the key can write files and nothing else.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Make a key for the extension

A key is the credential a program sends with each request. Give the extension a key of its own, so that it reaches only what it needs. In a terminal, make a key that reads and writes files:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa keys create --label "Raycast" --source raycast \
  --type-permission core.file=write
```

```text
marfa_k1_…
key 01a1f180-8448-7483-bc7b-658365a3a12f (Raycast); the plaintext is shown once, keep it now
  core.file  Read and edit
```

</Terminal>

<Callout type="warn" title="Copy the key now">Marfa shows it once. If you lose it, make a new one.</Callout>

The `--type-permission` flag names the one type the key may write, `core.file`. **That's also what lets it upload bytes**: Marfa takes an upload from a key that may write at least one type. The **source** is the label Marfa puts on every item the key creates, so you can always tell what the extension saved. [Manage keys](/use/manage-keys) explains each flag, and [Access](/build/access) explains what a key can hold.

</Step>
<Step>

### Create the extension and add the client

Open Raycast and run the **Create Extension** command. Name the extension "Marfa Capture", choose a template and a folder. Then, in the new folder, add the Marfa client and Raycast's utilities:

```bash
npm install @withmarfa/client @raycast/utils
```

The [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) is a typed client for every operation. It knows each path, parameter and answer, so a mistake in a request fails the type check.

The extension needs to know where your instance is and which key to use. In `package.json`, replace the template's `commands` with one command, and add two **preferences**:

```json title="package.json"
{
  "platforms": ["macOS"],
  "commands": [
    {
      "name": "save-file",
      "title": "Save File",
      "description": "Save a file to Marfa",
      "mode": "view"
    }
  ],
  "preferences": [
    {
      "name": "apiUrl",
      "title": "Server URL",
      "description": "Where your Marfa instance answers, such as http://localhost:8600",
      "type": "textfield",
      "required": true
    },
    {
      "name": "apiKey",
      "title": "API Key",
      "description": "A key made for this extension",
      "type": "password",
      "required": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Raycast runs a command from the file in `src` that its `name` gives, so this one runs `src/save-file.tsx`. Delete the template's own command file. Leave the rest of the template's `package.json` and `tsconfig.json` as they are.

Raycast asks for a required preference before the command first runs, and a `password` preference is for secure entry.

</Step>
<Step>

### Keep every call in one module

Put each request to Marfa in one file. The rest of the extension then asks for a saved file, and never sees a URL or a key:

```ts title="src/marfa.ts"
import { getPreferenceValues } from "@raycast/api";
import { createClient } from "@withmarfa/client";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { basename, extname } from "node:path";

/** What the server said when it refused a request. */
export class MarfaError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    readonly code: string,
    message: string,
  ) {
    super(message);
  }
}

function client() {
  const { apiUrl, apiKey } = getPreferenceValues<Preferences>();
  return createClient({ baseUrl: apiUrl.trim(), credential: apiKey.trim() });
}

type Refusal = { error: { code: string; message: string } };

function refused(response: Response, refusal: Refusal) {
  return new MarfaError(response.status, refusal.error.code, refusal.error.message);
}

// The media type each kind of file is stored under. Anything else is
// stored as plain bytes.
const mediaTypes: Record<string, string> = {
  ".pdf": "application/pdf",
  ".png": "image/png",
  ".jpg": "image/jpeg",
  ".jpeg": "image/jpeg",
  ".txt": "text/plain",
  ".md": "text/markdown",
  ".csv": "text/csv",
};

export async function saveFile(path: string, title: string, notes: string) {
  const marfa = client();
  const upload = await marfa.POST("/blobs", {
    body: await readFile(path),
    headers: { "Content-Type": mediaTypes[extname(path).toLowerCase()] ?? "application/octet-stream" },
  });
  if (upload.error) throw refused(upload.response, upload.error);
  const { hash, mime_type } = upload.data;

  const properties: Record<string, unknown> = { blob_ref: hash, mime_type, title: title || basename(path) };
  if (notes) properties.notes = notes;
  const { data, error, response } = await marfa.POST("/items", {
    body: { type: "core.file", properties },
  });
  if (error) throw refused(response, error);
  return data.item;
}
```

Saving a file takes two requests:

1. [Upload a blob](/reference/api/blobs/uploadBlob) sends the bytes as they are, with their media type as the `Content-Type`. Marfa answers the bytes' `hash` and the `mime_type` it stores them under. That's the type the bytes were first uploaded with, so the item takes it from the answer.
2. [Create an item](/reference/api/items/createItem) saves a `core.file` that names the bytes. A file item requires `blob_ref`, the hash, and `mime_type`. The title falls back to the file's name.

Each call returns `data` when it works and `error` when Marfa refuses it. A refusal carries a stable `code` and a `message` for people, so `MarfaError` keeps both. Raycast generates the `Preferences` type from your `package.json`, in `raycast-env.d.ts`, so don't write it yourself. [Files](/build/files) explains how a blob and the item that names it fit together.

</Step>
<Step>

### Build the form and save the file

Create `src/save-file.tsx` with a form that picks one file and takes a title and notes:

```tsx title="src/save-file.tsx"
import { Action, ActionPanel, Form, popToRoot, showToast, Toast } from "@raycast/api";
import { MarfaError, saveFile } from "./marfa";

type Values = { files: string[]; title: string; notes: string };

export default function SaveFile() {
  async function save(values: Values) {
    const [path] = values.files;
    if (!path) {
      await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Failure, title: "Choose a file first" });
      return;
    }
    const toast = await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Animated, title: "Uploading" });
    try {
      const item = await saveFile(path, values.title.trim(), values.notes.trim());
      toast.style = Toast.Style.Success;
      toast.title = "Saved";
      toast.message = item.id;
      await popToRoot();
    } catch (error) {
      toast.style = Toast.Style.Failure;
      if (error instanceof MarfaError) {
        toast.title = `Refused: ${error.code}`;
        toast.message = error.message;
      } else {
        toast.title = "Could not reach Marfa";
        toast.message = String(error);
      }
    }
  }

  return (
    <Form
      actions={
        <ActionPanel>
          <Action.SubmitForm title="Save to Marfa" onSubmit={save} />
        </ActionPanel>
      }
    >
      <Form.FilePicker id="files" title="File" allowMultipleSelection={false} />
      <Form.TextField id="title" title="Title" placeholder="The file's name" />
      <Form.TextArea id="notes" title="Notes" />
    </Form>
  );
}
```

Each control's `id` names the value it fills. A file picker's value is a list of paths, even when it takes one file. The toast says **Uploading** while the bytes travel, then shows the new item's ID, or the server's `code` and `message` when Marfa refuses it. The file arrives with the `source` of the key, `raycast`. [File](/catalog/file) lists every field the type holds.

</Step>
<Step>

### Run the extension

In the extension's folder, check the types, then start the extension:

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run dev
```

`tsc` reports a type error with its file and line, and prints nothing when there's none. `npm run dev` starts the extension in development mode and adds it to the top of Raycast's root search.

Open Raycast and search for **Save File**. The first time, Raycast asks for the preferences. Enter your instance's address, such as `http://localhost:8600`, and paste the key from step 1. Choose a file, and run **Save to Marfa** from the form's actions. A **Saved** toast shows the new file's ID.

Check the file in the terminal, where the CLI is signed in to your instance:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items list --source raycast
```

```text
id                                    type       when                      title
01a1f181-edb3-75e6-8405-b7a0178c4cef  core.file  2026-11-19T01:53:06.483Z  kitchen-plan.txt
```

</Terminal>

`marfa items get` with that ID shows the `blob_ref`, the `mime_type` and the `size_bytes` Marfa set once it held the bytes.

You now have a Raycast command that saves files to your own instance, with a key that can do little else. Stop `npm run dev` in the terminal when you're done. The extension stays in Raycast.
